hints: Focus on where sodium and sulfur sit in Period 3, and remember how atomic size changes across a period.
Sodium is in Group 1 on the far left and sulfur is in Group 16 on the right, so think about which neutral atom has the stronger pull on its outer electrons.
Now think about the ions in Na2S, Na+ which loses its outer shell and S2- which gains electrons, and decide how that flips the size comparison.
walkthrough:
**Compare the neutral atoms**

Think of atomic radius across Period 3. Both $\text{Na}$ and $\text{S}$ use 3 shells, but sulfur has a much larger proton number.

Across a period: greater nuclear charge = stronger attraction = smaller atom. So $\text{Na}$ atom > $\text{S}$ atom.

**Work out what ions form**

Sodium loses one electron to get a noble gas octet, and sulfur gains two electrons:
$$\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{Na}^{+} + e^{-}$$
$$\text{S} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \text{S}^{2-}$$

**Compare the ionic radii**

$\text{Na}^{+}$ loses its whole n=3 shell and is left with just 2 shells (2,8). It also has more protons than electrons, so it shrinks a lot.

$\text{S}^{2-}$ keeps all 3 shells (2,8,8) and has extra electron-electron repulsion, so it swells larger than the S atom. Therefore $\text{Na}^{+}$ < $\text{S}^{2-}$.

**Combine both conclusions**

Atomic radius: sodium > sulfur. Ionic radius: sodium < sulfur. That matches one row in the table exactly.

options.A: Incorrect. It reverses the atomic trend. Across Period 3, sodium has fewer protons pulling on the same number of shells, so neutral Na is larger than neutral S, not smaller.
options.B: Incorrect. Both comparisons are wrong way round for atoms. Neutral Na is larger than S, and while the ionic part (sodium < sulfur) is true, the atomic part fails.
options.C: Incorrect. The atomic part is right (sodium > sulfur) but the ionic part is wrong. Students choosing this forget that Na+ loses a shell and shrinks, while S2- gains electrons and expands, so Na+ is much smaller than S2-.
options.D: Correct. Neutral Na > neutral S due to decreasing atomic radius across Period 3. But Na+ (2 shells, 10 electrons) is much smaller than S2- (3 shells, 18 electrons), so ionic sodium < sulfur.
